# Terminal Keys and Habits {#sec-terminal}

A handful of keys make the terminal much faster and less error-prone. They are defaults in Bash, Ubuntu's
shell, and zsh, the Mac's, and in Windows Terminal and the Mac's Terminal app (GNU Bash and zsh line-editor
manuals; Microsoft and Apple keyboard documentation; all checked 2026-10-31).

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| **Tab** | completes a file or command name; lists the choices when several match |
| **Up arrow** | brings back the previous command |
| **Ctrl+C** | stops the running command (in Windows Terminal, copies instead when text is selected) |
| **Ctrl+Shift+C**, **Ctrl+Shift+V** | copy and paste in Windows Terminal and Ubuntu (Mac: Command-C, Command-V) |
| right-click | in Windows Terminal: copies a selection, or pastes when nothing is selected |
| **Ctrl+A**, **Ctrl+E** | jump to the start and the end of the line |
| **Ctrl+U** | delete to the start of the line (the whole line in zsh); **Ctrl+K** deletes to the end |
| **Ctrl+L** | clear the screen |
| **Ctrl+R** | search earlier commands as you type; Ctrl+R again for older matches, Enter runs it, Ctrl+G gives up |

: Terminal keys worth knowing. {#tbl-terminal-keys}

::: pitfall
Ctrl+C in the assistant's tab interrupts the assistant, not a command. In Windows Terminal it copies only when
text is selected; with nothing selected it stops what is running.
:::

::: tryit
Open a second tab (Ctrl+Shift+D in Windows Terminal, Command-T on a Mac), type `ls ~/quarto-w` and press
**Tab**, then Enter. Press **Ctrl+L**, then **Ctrl+R** and type `ls`; then **Ctrl+A**, **Ctrl+E** and
**Ctrl+U**.

::: done
Ctrl+R found your `ls` command and Ctrl+U cleared it.
:::
:::

## Habits {.unnumbered}

- **Know where you are.** Run `pwd` before starting an assistant: its answer is the assistant's root folder
  (@sec-root-folder).
- **Two tabs.** Keep the assistant in one tab and commands such as `quarto preview` in another, both in the
  project folder.
- **New tab after installing.** A terminal learns where programs are when it starts, so a program installed
  a moment ago is "not found" until you open a new tab.
- **Read before you run.** Whether a command comes from the book, a web chat or the assistant, read it before
  you press Enter or approve it, especially anything with `sudo` or `rm`.
- **Copy errors whole.** When something fails, copy the command and the entire error text; the useful line is
  rarely the last one.
